newsitem.title: CHINA: HK charges Merrill Lynch man with money laundering.
newsitem.headline: HK charges Merrill Lynch man with money laundering.

text.p: Hong Kong police on Wednesday charged former Merrill Lynch banking star Kevin Wallace with a money laundering offence, a police spokesman said.

The spokesman told Reuters that Wallace was charged with "dealing with the proceeds of an indictable offence" under article 25 of Hong Kong's Organised and Serious Crimes Ordinance. Wallace will appear in court later in the day.

Wallace was detained 10 days ago along with an unidentified Chinese man in connection with an alleged fraud said to involve up to US$30 million. A former private banking star at Merrill Lynch, Wallace posted bail on July 9 of more than HK$1 million.
U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch International started civil proceedings against Wallace last month in Singapore and Hong Kong, and filed a criminal complaint in Singapore.

Merrill Lynch accused Wallace of engaging in "unauthorised trading, misrepresenting or falsifying private clients' statements and forging client signatures". In his job at Merrill, Wallace acted as a financial consultant to high-net worth clients across Asia, taking investment orders and providing investment advice.

The 46-year-old American was employed by Merrill Lynch from late 1991 until he was dismissed on May 15 this year. Merrill Lynch has not commented on the amount in question in the case, but industry sources and media reports have put it at around US$30 million.
